It finds the last newline among bytes actually read, excludes the unfinished tail, and hashes exactly that complete-line prefix. Appends beyond the captured high-water do not enter this snapshot.

The reader assumes append-only data; it does not lock the inode against same-file overwrites or provide a before/after preservation comparison. Its completeBytes may be less than highWaterBytes after a partial trailing record or short read. Thus acquisition establishes which complete bytes were read at one bounded observation, not that those bytes remained unchanged through launch, that later appends came from the source owner, or that source claims/wakes were preserved. D-017 requires the later exact-prefix comparison and independent target/launch/per-call/D006 actor evidence. No such after-comparison or actor-ledger audit was performed by this answering session. I also have not independently measured the serving build: 919b3798fa is the saved launch record's build value.

Established limitation: the native frame itself lacks the source identity/hash fields requested by the instruction, so source provenance needs the separately retained preparation/launch evidence. The matched checksum proves this target received that rendered frame; it does not prove raw-source immutability, universal same-UID/process isolation, a normal consult matrix, R6 acceptance, or shipment.
